models.purpose: Route each evacuee to the nearest usable exit.
models.summary: Each storey becomes an island and each staircase a bridge. Stairs between two storeys are bound together; the equivalent length is L over n and the equivalent width is W, with L = 100 m, W = 20 m and n = 3, 13, 28, 14 across the four floor pairs. The floor is discretized into nodes. The edge weight is the geometric distance when the nodes differ, lie within the visual range of 21 m and sit outside the deadly zone of radius 30 m; it is zero on the diagonal and infinity otherwise. Dijkstra is run once for each of the four exits and the shortest route is kept, unless that exit has already taken its cap. Average evacuation time is the total distance divided by the headcount times the sum of each group share times its speed. With 1471 people, shares 72.1, 21.1 and 6.8 percent and speeds 1.28, 1.03 and 0.78 m/s, the times are 364.85 s overall, 413.98 s elderly, 336.35 s young and 551.95 s disabled, over 6.33 times 10 to the 5 metres. Without a cap, 90 percent leave by exit 1; capping each exit at 50 percent relieves it.

models.purpose: Score each mesh by how dangerous it is right now.
models.summary: A mesh is the circle around a node. Its density weight is the headcount over pi times the mesh radius squared, its emergency weight is one over the distance to the danger source, and its exit weight is the distance to the nearest exit. The danger index is a weighted sum of the three, with weights a, b and c left free so the manager can raise the emergency weight early and lower it later. Additional exits open by a step rule: all n when the count of people in meshes above the threshold exceeds a, one fewer between b and a, and none when that count is near zero. The cutoffs are to be set by fuzzy sets or Monte Carlo, but no data are given and the paper does not compute them. Emergency personnel enter through the underused exits and move from low index to high index, the reverse of the evacuees.

models.purpose: Check the 2D plan against a 3D copy of the building.
models.summary: A 3D copy of the Louvre is drawn in AutoCAD and loaded into Pathfinder, which divides the indoor space into triangular cells. Two modes are available: SFPE, which behaves like the basic search, and Steering, which behaves like the danger index. The heat map of evacuation time per floor shows the same color trend as the 2D danger index, taken as indirect support. Bottlenecks sit near staircases and exits, though distant exits draw few people and do not become bottlenecks.
